title: Agreeing and disagreeing
about: How to agree, disagree politely and talk about arguments: share someone's view, see their point, come to a compromise, agree to differ, strongly disagree, a heated argument, a bitter dispute.

parts.title: Adjective and noun collocations for disputes and strong disagreements
Further collocations for agreeing and disagreeing

items.phrase: go along with an idea / a view
items.pattern: go along with an idea / a view / a plan / sb's suggestion
items.meaning: accept someone's idea or opinion, often without being very excited about it
items.example: I'd have preferred Italian, but I **went along with the idea** of trying the new Thai place.
more: My sister wanted to paint the hall yellow, and in the end we all **went along with her idea**.
I can't **go along with the view** that children should never eat sweets.
items.watchOut: Потрібні всі три слова: go along with the idea. Часто означає «погодитися, хоч і без захвату». Не плутай з get along with sb — ладнати з людиною.

items.pattern: be in (complete / total) agreement (with sb) (about / on / over sth) · be entirely in agreement
items.meaning: agree completely with someone; a little formal
items.example: My parents **are in complete agreement** about one thing: I need to tidy my room.
more: The neighbours **were in agreement** that the old tree in the shared garden should stay.
For once, my brother and I **are in total agreement**: pizza tonight.
items.watchOut: «Я згоден» — I agree, а не I am agree. Якщо хочеш сказати з be, потрібен іменник: I am in agreement with you.

items.pattern: tend to agree / disagree (with sb / that…)
items.meaning: a softer, more polite way of saying that you agree or disagree
items.uk: схилятися до думки, що…; радше погоджуватися / не погоджуватися
items.example: I **tend to agree** with your mum: a puppy is a lot of work in a small flat.
more: Everyone says the sequel is better, but I **tend to disagree**.
Most dentists **tend to agree** that children shouldn't have fizzy drinks.
items.watchOut: Tend to тут не про звичку, а пом'якшення: I tend to agree — «я радше погоджуюся». Звучить ввічливіше, ніж просто I agree чи I disagree.

items.pattern: share sb's opinion / view (that…) · share the opinion that…
items.meaning: have the same opinion as someone else
items.example: I **share your opinion** that the new bus timetable is a disaster.
more: Not everyone in the family **shares my view** that Christmas should start in November.
Many parents **share the opinion** that the school day is too long.
items.watchOut: I share your opinion — «я поділяю вашу думку» (думаю так само), без прийменника. А share your opinion with us — «поділіться з нами своєю думкою», тобто розкажіть її. «Поділяти» тут не divide.

items.pattern: appreciate sb's point of view (but…) · appreciate other people's points of view
items.meaning: understand why someone thinks something, even if you don't agree; often comes before 'but'
items.example: I **appreciate your point of view**, but I still think the party should end at midnight.
more: A good teacher **appreciates other people's points of view**.
I **appreciate your point of view**, Dad, but it's my money and my decision.
items.watchOut: Appreciate тут не «цінувати», а «розуміти»: I appreciate your point of view, but… — ввічливий вступ до незгоди. Точка зору — point of view, а не point of sight.

items.pattern: see sb's point · I (can) see your point (, but…)
items.meaning: understand what someone means and accept that it makes sense
items.uk: розуміти, що хтось має на увазі; розуміти чиюсь думку
items.example: OK, I **see your point**: if we leave at six, we'll miss the traffic.
more: When I showed him how much petrol costs, my son finally **saw my point**.
I can **see your point**: a smaller flat would be easier to clean.
items.watchOut: Тут see — «розуміти», як у «бачу, до чого ти ведеш». Кажуть see your point, зазвичай не see your thought чи see your idea. Британці також кажуть I take your point.

items.pattern: enter into an argument (with sb) (about / over sth)
items.meaning: become involved in an argument; rather formal
items.example: I refuse to **enter into an argument** with my uncle about politics at Christmas dinner.
more: The receptionist smiled and didn't **enter into an argument** about the booking.
Don't **enter into an argument** with a tired toddler. You won't win.
items.watchOut: Argument — передусім «суперечка, сварка», а не лише «аргумент». Вступити в суперечку — enter into an argument (офіційніше) або get into an argument (розмовне).

items.pattern: differences arise / exist (between A and B) (over / about sth) · differences of opinion
items.meaning: disagreements appear or are there between people
items.example: **Differences** often **arise** between flatmates over cleaning and bills.
more: Some **differences** still **exist** between my parents about how strict to be with us.
**Differences of opinion arose** at the meeting, but we found a solution.
items.watchOut: Розбіжності виникають — differences arise (arise – arose – arisen). Не плутай з rise (підніматися, зростати) і raise (піднімати щось).

items.pattern: come to / reach a compromise (with sb) (on / over sth)
items.meaning: agree on a solution in which each person gets part of what they wanted
items.example: The kids wanted pizza and we wanted soup, so we **came to a compromise**: pizza today, soup tomorrow.
more: My flatmate and I finally **reached a compromise** about the heating.
After a long phone call, the family **reached a compromise** on the holiday dates.
items.watchOut: Вимова: /ˈkɒmprəmaɪz/ — наголос на перший склад, у кінці «-майз», а не «-міс». Дійти компромісу — come to / reach a compromise. Make compromises — «йти на поступки», це трохи інше.

items.pattern: settle a dispute (with sb / between A and B) · a family / pay / border dispute
items.meaning: end a serious disagreement by finding a solution that both sides accept
items.example: The two neighbours **settled their dispute** about the fence over a cup of tea.
more: The new rota **settled the dispute** about who walks the dog.
It took months to **settle the dispute** with the builders over the leaking roof.
items.watchOut: Dispute — не «диспут» (наукова дискусія), а спір, конфлікт. Наголос на другий склад: /dɪˈspjuːt/. Залагодити спір — settle (або resolve) a dispute.

items.pattern: settle your / our / their differences (with sb)
items.meaning: stop disagreeing and find a way to get on with each other again
items.example: My aunt and my mum finally **settled their differences** after ten years of silence.
more: We **settled our differences** over a long walk and a coffee.
The two friends **settled their differences** and went on holiday together as planned.
items.watchOut: Differences тут у множині: settle our differences. «Владнати розбіжності» — зазвичай settle або resolve, а не decide чи solve our differences.

items.pattern: agree to differ (also agree to disagree)
items.meaning: accept that you have different opinions and stop trying to change each other's mind
items.example: Mum thought the film was boring and I loved it, so we **agreed to differ**.
more: My grandad and I **agree to differ** about pineapple on pizza.
The two teachers **agreed to differ** and moved on to the next point on the list.
items.watchOut: Залишитися кожен при своїй думці — agree to differ (британське) або agree to disagree. Не agree to be different.

items.pattern: entirely / wholeheartedly agree (with sb / that…) · agree entirely
items.meaning: agree completely; wholeheartedly also shows strong, warm support
items.example: I **entirely agree** with you: we should book the hotel now, before prices go up.
more: I **wholeheartedly agree** with the plan to keep the library open on Sundays.
I **agree entirely** that the train is less stressful than driving.
items.watchOut: Не I very agree: дієслово agree не підсилюють словом very. Кажуть I entirely / completely / totally agree або I very much agree. У wholeheartedly w не читається: /ˌhəʊlˈhɑːtɪdli/.

items.phrase: agree partly / up to a point
items.pattern: partly agree · agree (with sb) up to a point
items.meaning: agree with some of what someone says, but not all of it
items.example: I **agree up to a point**: walking to school is healthy, but not when it's pouring with rain.
more: I only **partly agree** with the doctor's advice to give up coffee.
My boss **agreed up to a point** and gave me two extra days off, not five.
items.watchOut: «До певної міри» — up to a point або to some extent. Не until a point: until — лише про час.

items.pattern: fundamentally / totally / strongly disagree (with sb) (about / over sth) · disagree fundamentally / strongly
items.meaning: disagree completely; fundamentally — about the most basic things, strongly — with strong feelings
items.example: My husband and I **fundamentally disagree** about how much screen time children need.
more: My best friend **strongly disagreed** when I said the book was better than the film.
The two coaches **totally disagree** about who should be captain.
items.watchOut: «Категорично не згоден» — I strongly / totally disagree. Зазвичай не кажуть I highly disagree і точно не I very disagree. Fundamentally — коли люди розходяться в самих основах.

items.pattern: a head-on clash (with sb / between A and B) (over sth)
items.meaning: a disagreement in which people confront each other directly and openly
items.uk: пряме (відкрите) зіткнення, конфлікт лоб у лоб
items.example: Tom and his manager had a **head-on clash** over working at weekends.
more: Try to avoid a **head-on clash** with a teenager. Talk when you've both calmed down.
There was a **head-on clash** between the two neighbours over the shared drive.
items.watchOut: «Лобове» зіткнення — head-on (буквально «лоб у лоб»), а не forehead. Не плутай з head-first — «головою вперед». Про машини кажуть a head-on collision, про людей у суперечці — a head-on clash.

items.pattern: a bitter dispute / argument / row (over / about sth)
items.meaning: an angry disagreement that goes on for a long time and leaves bad feelings
items.example: The family had a **bitter dispute** over Grandma's house, and the cousins stopped speaking.
more: A **bitter dispute** about noise went on between the two flats for years.
Their divorce turned into a **bitter row** about who would keep the dog.
items.watchOut: «Запеклий спір» — a bitter dispute (буквально «гіркий»: неприємний, як гіркий смак), а не hard dispute. Bitter також: a bitter argument, a bitter row, bitter enemies.

items.pattern: a heated argument / debate / discussion (about / over sth) · have a heated argument
items.meaning: an argument in which people get angry and excited
items.example: We had a **heated argument** about whose turn it was to wash up.
more: A **heated argument** broke out in the queue when someone pushed in.
The school meeting turned into a **heated debate** about uniforms.
items.watchOut: «Гаряча суперечка» — a heated argument, зазвичай не hot argument: hot — про температуру чи гостру їжу. Пам'ятай: argument — це «суперечка, сварка».

items.pattern: a fundamental disagreement (about / over sth) · have a fundamental disagreement
items.meaning: a disagreement about the most basic and important things
items.example: My friend and I have a **fundamental disagreement** about money: she saves, I spend.
more: There was a **fundamental disagreement** between the builders and the owners about the size of the kitchen.
Two of the partners left the firm after a **fundamental disagreement** about its future.
items.watchOut: «Принципова незгода» — a fundamental disagreement, а не principal disagreement: principal означає «головний» (the principal reason). Є й дієслово: fundamentally disagree.

items.pattern: reach a unanimous agreement (on sth) · a unanimous decision / vote · be unanimous
items.meaning: an agreement that every person in a group accepts
items.example: After a short vote, the residents reached a **unanimous agreement** to plant more trees in the courtyard.
more: The family reached a **unanimous agreement**: no phones at the dinner table.
It's rare for thirty teenagers to reach a **unanimous agreement** about anything.
items.watchOut: Вимова: /juˈnænɪməs/ — наголос на другий склад, на початку «ю», тому артикль a, а не an. Не плутай з anonymous (анонімний).

items.pattern: controversy rages / exists / continues to rage (over / about sth)
items.meaning: there is strong public disagreement about something, often angry and lasting a long time
items.example: **Controversy** still **rages** in our town over the new one-way system.
more: **Controversy** has **raged** for months over the plan for a new runway at the airport.
Little **controversy exists** about the benefits of a daily walk.
items.watchOut: Rage — «вирувати, лютувати», як буря чи пожежа: controversy rages — суперечки не вщухають. Наголос: британською /ˈkɒntrəvɜːsi/ (також /kənˈtrɒvəsi/).

items.pattern: a conflict of opinion (between / within…) · conflicting opinions
items.meaning: a situation where people in a group strongly disagree
items.example: A **conflict of opinion** between my parents means we still haven't booked our summer holiday.
more: There's a **conflict of opinion** in the office about whether to keep the windows open.
The two doctors gave me **conflicting opinions**, so I asked for a third.
items.watchOut: Конфлікт думок — a conflict of opinion (зазвичай однина opinion) або conflicting opinions. Наголос: іменник conflict — на перший склад /ˈkɒnflɪkt/, дієслово — на другий /kənˈflɪkt/.

warmup.uk: Ми з чоловіком цілком згодні щодо меню.
warmup.q: My husband and I are in complete ___ about the menu.
warmup.explain: Be in agreement — тут потрібен іменник agreement. «Я згоден» — просто I agree, а не I am agree.

warmup.uk: Я поділяю твою думку щодо нового сусіда.
warmup.q: I ___ your opinion about the new neighbour.
warmup.explain: Поділяти думку — share sb's opinion, без прийменника. Divide і split — ділити на частини.

warmup.q: In the end we ___ a compromise.
warmup.explain: Дійти компромісу — reach a compromise або come to a compromise.

warmup.uk: Давай просто залишимося кожен при своїй думці.
warmup.explain: Agree to differ (або agree to disagree) — визнати, що думки різні, і припинити суперечку.

warmup.uk: Я розумію, що ти маєш на увазі, але квитки надто дорогі.
warmup.q: I ___ your point, but the tickets are too expensive.
warmup.explain: See sb's point — розуміти чиюсь думку. Британці кажуть і I take your point.

warmup.uk: Учора в нас була гаряча суперечка про гроші.
warmup.q: We had a ___ argument about money yesterday.
warmup.explain: Гаряча суперечка — a heated argument, а не hot.

warmup.uk: Я категорично не згоден із цим правилом.
warmup.explain: Категорично не згоден — I strongly (totally) disagree. Highly і very з disagree зазвичай не вживають.

warmup.uk: У нас принципова розбіжність щодо виховання дітей.
warmup.q: We have a ___ disagreement about bringing up children.
warmup.explain: Принципова, докорінна розбіжність — a fundamental disagreement. Principal означає «головний».

A.q: My brother wanted to drive through the night, and in the end we ___ along with his plan.
A.explain: Go along with — погодитися з ідеєю чи планом. Get along with sb — ладнати з людиною.

A.q: We'll never agree about which film is better, so let's just agree to ___.
A.explain: Agree to differ (або agree to disagree) — залишитися кожен при своїй думці.

A.q: My housemate and I came ___ a compromise: she cooks and I wash up.
A.explain: Come to a compromise — дійти компромісу; також reach a compromise.

B.q: Gran agrees up to a ___: she'll use a mobile phone, but only for calls.
B.explain: Agree up to a point — погоджуватися певною мірою, частково.

B.q: Your idea is brilliant. I agree with it ___.
B.explain: Wholeheartedly agree — щиро, всім серцем погоджуватися. Heavily і highly з agree не вживають.

B.q: I ___ disagree with closing the playground. Where will the children play?
B.explain: Рішуче не згоден — I strongly disagree. Highly disagree — типова помилка.

C.q: The meeting about the new car park ended in a ___ argument.
C.explain: Гаряча суперечка — a heated argument (heat — нагрівати).

C.q: After a ___ dispute over the bill, the couple never went back to that restaurant.
C.explain: Запеклий спір — a bitter dispute: bitter (гіркий) — як неприємний смак.

C.q: My boss and I had a ___ clash over my holiday dates.
C.explain: A head-on clash — пряме, відкрите зіткнення, лоб у лоб.

D.q: The ___ agreement surprised everyone: even Uncle Bob said yes.
The ___ about the new speed bumps rages on in the local newspaper.
D.explain: Controversy rages — точаться гарячі суперечки. Contradiction — суперечність у словах чи фактах.

D.q: A ___ of opinion among the teachers has delayed the school trip.
D.explain: Розбіжність думок — a conflict of opinion.

example.title: Mountains or sea?
example.uk:
Щоліта в нашій родині спалахує гаряча суперечка про те, куди поїхати у відпустку. Цього року тато хотів у гори, мама — на море, і ніхто не хотів погоджуватися з чужою ідеєю.

Тоді заговорила бабуся. «Я розумію твою точку зору, — сказала вона татові, — але з хворим коліном тобі в гори не можна». Трохи подумавши, він зрозумів, що вона має рацію.

Зрештою ми дійшли компромісу: тиждень біля озера, а поруч невисокі пагорби. Ми з братом досі категорично не згодні щодо музики в машині, тож домовилися, що кожен залишиться при своїй думці. Зате щодо відпустки вся родина нарешті в повній згоді. Бабуся каже, що відтепер залагоджуватиме всі суперечки в цьому домі.
example.en:
Every summer my family has [[a heated argument|c3]] about where to go on holiday. This year Dad wanted the mountains and Mum wanted the sea, and nobody would [[go along with|a1]] anyone else's idea.

Then Gran spoke. 'I [[appreciate your point of view|a5]],' she told Dad, 'but you can't go climbing with a bad knee.' After a moment, he [[saw her point|a6]].

In the end we [[came to a compromise|a9]]: a week by a lake with gentle hills nearby. My brother and I still [[strongly disagree|b3]] about music in the car, so we've [[agreed to differ|a12]]. But about the holiday, the whole family is finally [[in complete agreement|a2]]. Gran says that from now on she will [[settle every dispute|a10]] in this house.
